summary: Qiagen said Wednesday it has agreed to a takeover offer from EQT Private Equity valued at 10.8 billion euros (about $12.1 billion), including approximately $1.1 billion of debt. The agreement comes less than two months after the testing company, long a rumored takeover target, installed Jonathan Pratt as its new CEO. Six years ago, Thermo Fisher Scientific was set to buy Qiagen, but the deal fell apart after shareholders objected to the price. William Blair analysts, in a Thursday note, said EQT’s all-cash offer of 46.50 euros per share (about $52.20) was reasonable, given Qiagen’s relatively lower growth profile.
title: Qiagen agrees to private equity takeover

summary: Edwards Lifesciences has won Food and Drug Administration approval for its Pascal Precision system for tricuspid valve repair, the company said Wednesday. Pascal’s expanded label covers use in patients with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation. Edwards previously received FDA approval for the device in degenerative mitral regurgitation. The approval should expand the group of tricuspid repair patients that Edwards can treat, Leerink Partners said in a note to investors.
title: Edwards wins FDA approval for tricuspid valve repair device

summary: Labcorp said Tuesday that it has agreed to acquire Myriad Genetics’ prenatal health testing business for $210 million. The deal covers tests for assessing fetal risk of certain conditions and other aspects of prenatal care. Labcorp expects the tests to add about $160 million in revenue in year one. Evercore ISI analysts see room for Labcorp to improve the economics of the acquired business using its infrastructure and to broaden access to the tests through its provider relationships.
title: Labcorp to buy Myriad’s prenatal health testing unit for $210M
